Clean bibliometric keywords

Source: R/keywords_clean.R
keywords_clean.Rd

Rewrites keyword columns (such as bibliometrix's `DE` and `ID`) so that one concept has one spelling. Every keyword is handled as a whole term, so its position in the list, the separator spacing, and characters such as `(`, `.` or `+` make no difference. In order:

1. **Cleanup**: HTML entities decoded, dashes and quotes unified, `&` written `AND`, a leading `#` dropped, spacing squeezed, upper case. 2. **Brackets**: a plural marker is dropped (`VOICE ASSISTANT(S)`); an acronym in brackets is dropped and remembered (`NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING (NLP)`, also `B-RNN (BI-DIRECTIONAL ...)`); other brackets lose only the bracket characters. 3. **Acronyms** (`expand_acronyms = TRUE`): a keyword that is exactly an acronym seen in brackets becomes its long form (`NLP` becomes `NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING`), but only when no other keyword in the data spells the same initials (`HRI` stays when both `HUMAN-ROBOT INTERFACE` and `HUMAN-ROBOT INTERACTION` occur). 4. **Replace**: whole-term `OLD` to `NEW` replacements from `replace`, cleaned the same way; chains (`A` to `B`, `B` to `C`) resolve to the last term, and a later row overrides an earlier one that contradicts it. 5. **Merge similar** (`merge_similar = TRUE`): keywords that differ only by plural, hyphen, space or punctuation (`CHAT BOT`, `CHAT-BOT`, `CHATBOTS`) become one: a `NEW` term from `replace` if one is among them, else the form in most papers. 6. **Drop** the `drop` keywords, then keep each keyword once per paper.

Usage

keywords_clean(
  data,
  columns = "DE",
  replace = NULL,
  drop = NULL,
  merge_similar = TRUE,
  expand_acronyms = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per paper. The result of another `clean_*()` function works too, so the cleaners chain: `M |> authors_clean(scopus = "Dlds") |> keywords_clean()`.

columns

Names of the keyword columns, `;`-separated. Default `"DE"` (bibliometrix's author keywords); `c("DE", "ID")` adds index keywords.

replace

Your replacement table: a data frame with columns `OLD` and `NEW` (more columns are ignored), or the path to a `.csv`, `.xlsx` or `.xls` file holding one. An [ask_ai()] result also works (its pairs with `decision` `accept` are applied), and so does a review sheet from [review_sheet()] (pairs whose `decision_2`, or else `decision`, is `accept`). Several tables or paths are applied in order, so a later table corrects an earlier one; within a table a later row overrides an earlier one. Reading `.xlsx`/`.xls` needs readxl.

drop

Keywords to delete, e.g. `c("SURVEY", "CASE STUDY")`. Similar spellings are deleted too (`"SURVEY"` also drops `SURVEYS`).

merge_similar

Merge keywords that differ only by plural, hyphen, space or punctuation? Default `TRUE`.

expand_acronyms

Expand a keyword that is an acronym into the long form found in brackets elsewhere in the data? Default `TRUE`.

Value

A `saqr_keywords` object. Use `as.data.frame()` on it:

  • `as.data.frame(x)`: `data` with the keyword columns rewritten, `"; "`-separated, each keyword once per paper.

  • `as.data.frame(x, what = "changes")`: one row per keyword that changed, most papers first: `column`, `from` (as written in `data`), `to` (`NA` when dropped), `reason` (`cleanup`, `brackets`, `acronym`, `replaced`, `merged`, `dropped`, joined by `+`) and `papers`.

  • `as.data.frame(x, what = "terms")`: one row per cleaned keyword, most papers first: `column`, `keyword`, `papers` and `forms` (how many written forms it gathers).

`summary()` returns one row per column with counts.

Errors

Raises `saqrmisc_bad_input` for a missing or non-character keyword column, a `replace` table without `OLD` and `NEW`, or a `replace` file that does not exist or is not `.csv`/`.xlsx`/`.xls`; `saqrmisc_missing_package` for an `.xlsx` file without readxl. Warns `saqrmisc_replace_conflict`, listing each row, when rows are overridden by a later row: the same `OLD` with another `NEW`, or a loop (`A` to `B` above `B` to `A`).

Examples

papers <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  DE = c("CHATBOT;  NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING (NLP);  AI",
         "CHAT-BOTS;  NLP;  ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE",
         "CHATBOTS;  E-LEARNING;  SURVEY")
)
my_table <- data.frame(OLD = "ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE", NEW = "AI")
cleaned <- keywords_clean(papers, replace = my_table, drop = "SURVEY")
cleaned
#> Keyword cleaning
#>   DE: 9 written forms became 4 keywords in 3 papers (1 replaced, 2 merged, 1 acronyms expanded, 1 dropped)
#> as.data.frame(x) gives the cleaned papers; keywords_changes(x) lists every change.
as.data.frame(cleaned)
#>   id                                       DE
#> 1  1 CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING; AI
#> 2  2 CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING; AI
#> 3  3                      CHATBOT; E-LEARNING
